notes:
Source: Colorado Time Systems, "Swimming 6" Software User Guide for the System 6 Sports Timer (Part No. F870, Rev. 2024-11-07), section "System 6 Back Panel" / Figure 2-H "System 6 I/O Panel," official manual hosted at coloradotime.com. Cross-checked against the manufacturer's System 6 product brochure (Rev 03/19, also distributed by dealer scoreboards.com) for physical dimensions, weight, power, and USB details.

Product is a swim/dive/water-polo/pace-clock timing and scoring console, not conventional broadcast/display AV gear, so several ports required approximation against the given AV-oriented connector taxonomy (flagged per-port above): the external power DIN, Judges I/O DIN, PS/2 mouse/keyboard mini-DIN, and parallel printer port all lack exact matches in the allowed connector list.

OMITTED from the port list: the console's primary signal inputs — Near-End and Far-End touchpad/start-system/backup-button cable-harness connectors (multiple large proprietary multi-pin connectors per the I/O-panel diagram, covering lanes 1-10 plus extra connectors for lanes 11-12 and a duplicate near/far pair for a second backup timer). These use a proprietary Colorado Time Systems multi-pin harness connector with no reasonable match among the allowed connector ids, so including them would have required a misleading choice.

Physical form factor: desktop/portable clamshell unit (laptop-like, hinged screen over keyboard), not rack-mountable — 9.75" x 18.38" x 11.5" (H x W x D), 10 lbs, durable molded plastic construction, UL certified. rackUnits omitted accordingly.

Power (per brochure, for the external AC-DC power brick that feeds the console's DIN power input): 120/220V, 50/60Hz, 0.8A. Includes an internal rechargeable battery for power-outage backup.

No bandwidth/version grades apply to any listed port (no HDMI/SDI/DisplayPort/USB-speed/Ethernet-speed figures are stated anywhere in the source), so grade was omitted throughout per instructions.

Colorado Time Systems has since introduced a newer "Gen 7" console line; System 6 appears to be a legacy/still-supported product (software user guide revised as recently as November 2024).

ports.name: External Power
ports.note: Console manual specifies a DIN connector from an approved external 15V DC power supply (P/N R-920-004); mapped to dc-barrel as the closest listed DC-power connector — actual plug is a locking DIN, not a coaxial barrel jack.

ports.name: Judges I/O
ports.note: DIN connector accepting input from judging expansion hardware (e.g. diving wireless judging interface) and other sport expansion I/O; mapped to midi-din as the closest DIN-family option — not an actual MIDI port.

ports.name: Scoreboard
ports.note: Manual describes a locking quarter-inch (6.35mm) jack carrying proprietary serial scoreboard data, not audio.

ports.name: COM Port 1
ports.note: 9-pin D-sub RS-232 serial port for a computer running meet management software.

ports.name: COM Port 2
ports.note: 9-pin D-sub RS-232 serial port used for TV broadcast data output. Not present on units built after 2024-11-07 per the manual.

ports.name: Printer Port
ports.note: Manual states this is a standard IBM PC parallel (Centronics/DB-25) port. No parallel-port connector exists in the given taxonomy; approximated to rs232 (closest D-sub family) — physical connector actually has 25 pins.

ports.name: Monitor
ports.note: Standard VGA output mirroring the console's own screen to an external monitor.

ports.name: Mouse
ports.note: Standard IBM PC PS/2 mouse connector (6-pin mini-DIN); approximated to midi-din as the closest DIN-family connector in the taxonomy — not an actual MIDI port.

ports.name: Keyboard
ports.note: Standard IBM PC PS/2 keyboard connector (6-pin mini-DIN); approximated to midi-din as the closest DIN-family connector in the taxonomy — not an actual MIDI port.

ports.name: USB Port
ports.note: Used for storage to a USB device or to connect a USB printer (newer units).

ports.name: Ethernet Port
ports.note: Used for online software updates. Link speed not stated in source, so no bandwidth grade set.
